text.p: Hurricane Marco continues as a significant risk to shipping in the Caribbean today and Thursday. Winds are now 75 mph and they may reach 85 mph on Thursday. The system is currently about 290 miles south-southwest of Jamaica. Marco is expected to spread heavy rain and wind through Jamaica, far east Cuba and Hispanola later in this period. Rain will likely lead to flooding and possibly mudslides. Strong winds and a coastal storm surge should cause problems as well, especially just east of the storm track.

The storm currently in the Netherlands will move to southeast Sweden by late Thursday. Strong winds in the English Channel and southern North Sea will diminish some as the storm exits the area. Strong winds may lead to problems in the Baltic sea during Thursday and Friday.

Rain in the Pacific northwest (USA) has diminished. Floods will continue for several more days. A new storm hits the west coast Thursday, this one further south. This may lead to some flooding in California mountains.
THERE ARE NO FURTHER EMERGENCY WEATHER STATEMENTS
